title: Inclined Plane Slider
description:
Create a class called `Slider` that simulates an object sliding down an inclined plane (ramp).

The class should be initialized with:
- angle: the angle of the incline (in degrees, between 0 and 90)
- length: the length of the ramp (in meters)
- friction: coefficient of kinetic friction (default 0.1, between 0 and 1)

The class should provide these methods:
- update(dt): Update the slider's state after a time step dt (in seconds)
- get_position(): Return distance traveled along the ramp (in meters)
- get_velocity(): Return current velocity along the ramp (in m/s)
- get_acceleration(): Return current acceleration along the ramp (in m/s²)
- has_reached_bottom(): Return True if the slider has reached the bottom (position >= length)
- get_time(): Return total time elapsed (in seconds)

Physics background:
- On an incline, gravity has a component along the ramp that accelerates the object downward
- Friction opposes motion and depends on the normal force (the force perpendicular to the surface)
- The net acceleration determines how the object speeds up
- If friction is strong enough, the object may not slide at all
- Use g = 9.8 m/s² for gravity
- Angles need conversion from degrees to radians

The slider starts from rest at the top of the ramp (position = 0).
